name: cost-management

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: An attacker could exploit overly permissive IAM roles or misconfigured secrets access policies to retrieve cloud credentials stored in Secrets Manager.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: A compromised Lambda function with excessive permissions could access Secrets Manager and retrieve credentials for all cloud providers, leading to unauthorized access across multiple cloud environments.

recommendations.description: Implement strict IAM policies following the principle of least privilege
recommendations.implementationDetails: Configure IAM roles to limit Secrets Manager access to only the Cost Collector Lambda function and implement resource-level permissions

recommendations.description: Implement AWS Organizations SCPs as recommended by security engineer
recommendations.implementationDetails: Create SCPs that restrict access to Secrets Manager actions and limit credential access to specific roles

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Use AWS Organizations SCPs to implement preventive controls, AWS CloudTrail for auditing all Secrets Manager and IAM activities, and AWS Config to monitor policy changes.

ground_truth.threatName: Sensitive Cost Data Exposure via S3

mitreATT&CK: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Misconfigured S3 bucket policies or inadequate access controls could allow unauthorized access to sensitive cost data stored in the buckets.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker could exploit overly permissive bucket policies to access or modify cost data, potentially leading to data leakage or manipulation of cost reports.

recommendations.description: Implement comprehensive S3 bucket security controls
recommendations.implementationDetails: Enable S3 Block Public Access, implement bucket policies with least privilege, enable encryption at rest, and implement access logging

recommendations.description: Implement data classification and handling controls
recommendations.implementationDetails: Tag sensitive data, implement lifecycle policies, and use S3 Object Lock for critical cost data

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Use AWS Macie for sensitive data discovery, S3 Block Public Access at account level, and AWS Config rules to monitor bucket configurations.

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Insufficient API Gateway authentication configuration or vulnerabilities in the authentication mechanism could allow unauthorized access to the API endpoints.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker could forge or manipulate authentication tokens to gain unauthorized access to cost management APIs.

recommendations.implementationDetails: Use AWS Cognito or custom Lambda authorizers, implement JWT validation, and enforce strong authentication policies

recommendations.description: Implement API request throttling and monitoring
recommendations.implementationDetails: Configure usage plans, API keys, and implement rate limiting to prevent abuse

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Use AWS WAF with API Gateway for additional protection, implement AWS Shield for DDoS protection, and use CloudWatch for monitoring authentication failures.

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Overly permissive IAM policies or compromised Lambda functions could allow unauthorized modification of cost data in DynamoDB.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker with access to a compromised Lambda function could modify cost data to hide resource usage or manipulate billing information.

recommendations.implementationDetails: Use IAM policies with least privilege, implement condition keys, and enable DynamoDB encryption
Enable DynamoDB streams for audit trails, implement checksums for critical data, and use versioning

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Use DynamoDB encryption at rest, enable Point-in-Time Recovery for data protection, and implement CloudWatch alerts for suspicious access patterns.

vulnerabilityDetails.howItWorks: Attackers with IAM permissions could modify EventBridge rules to disrupt cost data collection timing or frequency.
vulnerabilityDetails.exploitationScenario: An attacker could modify scheduling rules to prevent cost data collection or overwhelm the system with too frequent collections.

recommendations.implementationDetails: Use IAM policies to restrict EventBridge rule modifications to authorized roles only
Set up CloudWatch alerts for EventBridge rule modifications and failed executions

ground_truth.awsSpecificConsiderations: Use AWS Organizations SCPs to restrict EventBridge permissions, implement AWS Config rules to monitor rule changes, and use CloudTrail for audit logging.

#!/usr/bin/env python3

"""
AWS Serverless Multi-cloud Cost Management System
This diagram illustrates a serverless architecture for managing and analyzing
costs across multiple cloud providers, with secure API access and automated
data processing pipelines.
"""

# --- Analytics related imports ---
from diagrams.aws.analytics import Quicksight
from diagrams.aws.cost import CostExplorer, CostAndUsageReport

# --- Network related imports ---
from diagrams.aws.network import APIGateway

# --- Compute related imports ---
from diagrams.aws.compute import Lambda

# --- Integration related imports ---
from diagrams.aws.integration import Eventbridge

# --- Security related imports ---
from diagrams.aws.security import IAM, SecretsManager

# --- Storage related imports ---
from diagrams.aws.storage import S3

# --- Database related imports ---
from diagrams.aws.database import Dynamodb

# --- Management and Governance related imports ---
from diagrams.aws.management import Cloudwatch, Organizations

# --- General diagram imports ---
from diagrams import Diagram, Cluster, Edge
from diagrams.aws.general import Users

# Graph attributes for better visualization
graph_attr = {
    "fontsize": "45",
    "bgcolor": "white",
    "splines": "polyline",
    "pad": "2.0",
    "nodesep": "1.0",
    "ranksep": "1.2",
    "labelloc": "t",
    "label": "AWS Multi-cloud Cost Management System",
    "fontname": "Helvetica",
}

# Edge attributes for better label placement
edge_attr = {
    "minlen": "1.5",
    "labelangle": "0",
    "labeldistance": "2.0"
}

# Create the diagram
with Diagram(
    name="Serverless Multi-cloud Cost Management",
    filename="cost_management",
    direction="TB",
    show=True,
    graph_attr=graph_attr,
    edge_attr=edge_attr,
    outformat="png"
):
    # External Users
    users = Users("Cloud Admins")
    
    # AWS Account Boundary
    with Cluster("AWS Account Boundary", graph_attr={"style": "dashed", "color": "#FF9900", "bgcolor": "#FFFAF0"}):
        # Frontend Layer
        with Cluster("Frontend Services"):
            dashboard = Quicksight("Cost Dashboard")
        
        # API Layer
        with Cluster("API Layer"):
            api = APIGateway("Cost Management API")
            auth = IAM("Authentication")
        
        # Data Collection Layer
        with Cluster("Data Collection"):
            cost_explorer = CostExplorer("Cost Explorer")
            cost_reports = CostAndUsageReport("Usage Reports")
            org = Organizations("AWS Organizations")
            
            # Data Processing
            with Cluster("Processing Pipeline"):
                collector = Lambda("Cost Collector")
                processor = Lambda("Cost Processor")
                analyzer = Lambda("Cost Analyzer")
        
        # Data Storage Layer
        with Cluster("Data Storage"):
            raw_bucket = S3("Raw Cost Data")
            processed_bucket = S3("Processed Data")
            cost_db = Dynamodb("Cost Database")
        
        # Integration & Monitoring
        scheduler = Eventbridge("Scheduler")
        secrets = SecretsManager("Cloud Credentials")
        monitor = Cloudwatch("Monitoring")

    # Define connections with sequential flow
    
    # User Interactions
    users >> Edge(label="1. Access Dashboard", color="#000080") >> dashboard
    users >> Edge(label="2. API Request", color="#000080") >> api
    
    # Authentication
    api >> Edge(label="3. Verify", color="#000080") >> auth
    
    # Data Collection
    scheduler >> Edge(label="4. Schedule", color="#000080") >> collector
    collector >> Edge(label="5. Get Credentials", color="#000080") >> secrets
    collector >> Edge(label="6. Fetch AWS Costs", color="#000080") >> cost_explorer
    collector >> Edge(label="7. Get AWS Reports", color="#000080") >> cost_reports
    collector >> Edge(label="8. Query Org Data", color="#000080") >> org
    collector >> Edge(label="9. Fetch Other Cloud Costs", style="dashed", color="#000080") >> Edge(label="(Azure, GCP, etc.)")
    
    # Data Processing
    collector >> Edge(label="10. Save", color="#000080", fontsize="14", labelbgcolor="white") >> raw_bucket
    raw_bucket >> Edge(label="11. Process", color="#000080", fontsize="14", labelbgcolor="white") >> processor
    processor >> Edge(label="12. Analyze", color="#000080") >> analyzer
    
    # Data Storage
    analyzer >> Edge(label="13. Store", color="#000080") >> processed_bucket
    analyzer >> Edge(label="14. Update", color="#000080") >> cost_db
    
    # Dashboard Updates
    processed_bucket >> Edge(label="15. Load", color="#000080") >> dashboard
    cost_db >> Edge(label="16. Sync", color="#000080") >> dashboard
    
    # Single monitoring connection
    analyzer >> Edge(label="17. Monitor", style="dotted", color="#800000") >> monitor
    
    # Single IAM connection
    auth >> Edge(label="18. Authorize", style="dashed", color="#006400") >> api
